verses.english: Linked Discourses 36.8
1. With Verses
The Infirmary (2nd)

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena gilānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
verses.english: Then in the late afternoon, the Buddha came out of retreat and went to the infirmary, where he sat down on the seat spread out,
and addressed the mendicants:
“Mendicants, a mendicant should await their time mindful and aware.
This is my instruction to you.
And how is a mendicant mindful?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …
They meditate observing an aspect of the mind …

verses.pali: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: They meditate observing an aspect of principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sato hoti.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant is mindful.
And how is a mendicant aware?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu abhikkante paṭikkante sampajānakārī hoti …pe… bhāsite tuṇhībhāve sampajānakārī hoti.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant acts with situational awareness when going out and coming back; when looking ahead and aside; when bending and extending the limbs; when bearing the outer robe, bowl and robes; when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting; when urinating and defecating; when walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and keeping silent.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sampajāno hoti.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant is aware.

verses.pali: Sato, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sampajāno kālaṁ āgameyya.
verses.english: A mendicant should await their time mindful and aware.
This is my instruction to you.

verses.pali: Tassa ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno evaṁ satassa sampajānassa appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato uppajjati sukhā vedanā.
verses.english: While a mendicant is meditating like this—mindful, aware, diligent, keen, and resolute—if pleasant feelings arise, they understand:
‘A pleasant feeling has arisen in me.

verses.pali: sā ca kho paṭicca, no appaṭicca.
verses.english: That’s dependent, not independent.
Dependent on what?
Dependent on this very contact.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ kho pana phasso anicco saṅkhato paṭiccasamuppanno.
verses.english: But this contact is impermanent, conditioned, dependently originated.

verses.pali: Aniccaṁ kho pana saṅkhataṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ phassaṁ paṭicca uppannā sukhā vedanā kuto niccā bhavissatī’ti.
verses.english: So how could a pleasant feeling be permanent, since it has arisen dependent on contact that is impermanent, conditioned, and dependently originated?’

verses.pali: So phasse ca sukhāya ca vedanāya aniccānupassī viharati, vayānupassī viharati, virāgānupassī viharati, nirodhānupassī viharati, paṭinissaggānupassī viharati.
verses.english: They meditate observing impermanence, vanishing, dispassion, cessation, and letting go in contact and pleasant feeling.

verses.pali: Tassa phasse ca sukhāya ca vedanāya aniccānupassino viharato, vayānupassino viharato, virāgānupassino viharato, nirodhānupassino viharato, paṭinissaggānupassino viharato yo phasse ca sukhāya ca vedanāya rāgānusayo, so pahīyati.
verses.english: As they do so, they give up the underlying tendency for greed for contact and pleasant feeling.

verses.pali: Tassa ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno evaṁ satassa …pe…
verses.english: While a mendicant is meditating like this—mindful, aware, diligent, keen, and resolute—if painful feelings arise …
if neutral feelings arise, they understand:
‘A neutral feeling has arisen in me.

verses.pali: sā ca kho paṭicca, no appaṭicca.
verses.english: That’s dependent, not independent.
Dependent on what?
Dependent on this very contact.
(Tell in full as in the previous discourse.)

verses.pali: Kāyassa bhedā uddhaṁ jīvitapariyādānā idheva sabbavedayitāni anabhinanditāni sītībhavissantī’ti pajānāti.
verses.english: They understand: ‘When my body breaks up and my life is over, everything that’s felt, since I no longer take pleasure in it, will become cool right here.’

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, telañca paṭicca vaṭṭiñca paṭicca telappadīpo jhāyeyya,
verses.english: Suppose an oil lamp depended on oil and a wick to burn.

verses.pali: tasseva telassa ca vaṭṭiyā ca pariyādānā anāhāro nibbāyeyya;
verses.english: As the oil and the wick are used up, it would be extinguished due to not being fed.

verses.pali: evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāyapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vedayamāno ‘kāyapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti. Jīvitapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vedayamāno ‘jīvitapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti.
verses.english: In the same way, feeling the end of the body draw close, a mendicant understands: ‘I feel the end of the body draw close.’ Feeling the end of life draw close, they understand: ‘I feel the end of life draw close.’

verses.pali: ‘Kāyassa bhedā uddhaṁ jīvitapariyādānā idheva sabbavedayitāni anabhinanditāni sītībhavissantī’ti pajānātī”ti.
verses.english: They understand: ‘When my body breaks up and my life is over, everything that’s felt, since I no longer take pleasure in it, will become cool right here.’”
